title: Wiener Schnitzel
subtitle: crisp breaded veal or pork cutlet
excerpt: Wiener Schnitzel is a thin cutlet coated in fine breadcrumbs and fried in butter until golden and crisp. The hallmark is a rippled, souffle-like crust that puffs away from the meat during frying. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: The canonical Austrian dish, protected by name in Austria where it must use veal. Pork schnitzel is the everyday version across Germany and Austria.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bread the cutlets up to 1 hour ahead and refrigerate uncovered.

glossaryTerms.definition: To coat food in flour, egg wash, and breadcrumbs before frying to create a crisp outer crust.
To cook food in enough fat to come halfway up the sides of the item, giving a crisp result without full submersion.

content.text: the cutlets loosely so the crust can puff during frying, then
in plenty of hot butter, moving the pan constantly to keep the fat rolling over the surface. Serves 4.
Pork loin works beautifully here and is far more affordable than veal. Either way, pound the cutlets very thin, no more than 4mm.
Place each cutlet between two sheets of cling film. Pound with a rolling pin to an even 4mm thickness. Season lightly.

Set up three shallow dishes: flour in the first, beaten eggs in the second, breadcrumbs in the third. Press each cutlet into the flour, shaking off any excess. Dip in egg, letting it drip. Press lightly into breadcrumbs. Do not press hard: keep the crumbs loose.
Heat the butter and oil together in a large frying pan over medium-high heat until the butter foams and the foam begins to subside.
Lay in one or two cutlets and gently swirl the pan so the fat washes up over the crust. Fry for 2 to 3 minutes each side until deep golden. The crust should ripple and puff. Drain on kitchen paper.
Cook the remaining cutlets, adding more butter if needed. Serve immediately with lemon wedges.
The fat was not hot enough. Get it properly shimmering before adding the cutlet, and swirl the pan rather than pressing down.
You pressed the breadcrumbs too firmly. Apply them with a light touch and do not compact them.
Pound the cutlets thinner next time. At 4mm they cook in 2 to 3 minutes per side. If they are thicker, lower the heat slightly and give them an extra minute.

Schnitzel is eaten all over Austria and Germany and turns up on menus from Vienna to Munich. It is a dish that depends entirely on technique, not exotic ingredients. The name Wiener means 'Viennese'. Lemon wedges and potato salad are the classic accompaniments.
